messages:
alex: Quick sync — saw a reproducible read-after-write gap when we demote a prefix and immediately hand it off. Repro steps below, have a proposed handshake sketch.

maria: Ugh, saw that too during the tenancy rebalance test. Can you paste the minimal repro?

alex: Repro: 1) client writes X to prefix P (short seq) 2) P is demoted locally and ownership moves to other shard 3) requester reads immediately after, gets stale value (missing X). Happens when demote happens before we flush new writes to remote snapshot.

chen: Sounds like a visibility window during demote where KV writes live in local pending buffer that doesn't get pushed. Are we flushing on demote?

alex: Current flow: demote -> revoke residency -> transfer metadata token -> new owner reads snapshot which may not include in-flight local writes. We tried quick flush but it's racy.

sam: My two cents: we need a two-phase demote handshake: 1) prepare (quiesce writers and grab demote-epoch) 2) commit (transfer epoch + stable tail). That guarantees any writer with epoch <= demote-epoch is durable.

maria: Can you sketch API-level changes? I want to understand implications for RPC surface and perf.

alex: Rough sketch: add demote_epoch to the ownership message. On prepare, owner returns a settle_token that encodes last_applied_seq and durability marker. New owner must wait until it sees durability >= settle_token before accepting reads for that prefix. Pseudocode:

```
// owner A
prepare_demote(prefix P):
  pause_local_writes(P)
  let settle_token = durable_tail(P) // persisted seq
  return settle_token

// owner B
accept_ownership(P, settle_token):
  fast-path: if local_snapshot >= settle_token then install ownership
  else block reads until catchup: apply_remote_log_until(settle_token)
```

alex: This avoids a full stop-the-world flush and instead relies on the durable_tail we already track.

chen: Nice. Questions: 1) who blocks what? Writers on old owner pause, but does client-level writer get a retry? 2) does this add latency to handoffs?

sam: For (1) writers should get 409/retry or a lightweight pause that the SDK can retry. We shouldn't block client forever. (2) Depends on how far behind new owner is. That's why we should prefer canary and avoid large transfers during hot moves.

maria: What about multi-tenant fairness? If new owner blocks waiting on a large settle_token from a previous hot writer, we could stall many small tenants. Maybe add an adjustable timeout and fallback to serving stale reads with a strong-staleness flag? We need policy knobs.

alex: Agreed. Propose policy: default is strong-consistency (block until durable_tail seen or timeout 5s), then degrade to serve-from-cache with stale-warning metric if timeout. Enterprise can configure stricter SLOs.

chen: Metrics we need to track for rollout: demote_handoff_latency, demote_block_count, read-after-write-failures, stale_read_served_count. Also histogram of settle_token_gap (how many ops needed to catch up).

sam: Test plan: - unit: simulate demote during concurrent writes - integration: canary on non-prod shard with synthetic clients that write+read tight loop - chaos: kill owner mid-prepare to ensure new owner recovers token and proceeds.

alex: Rolling upgrade notes: 1) older nodes ignore demote_epoch (compat) and will continue current behavior -> possible R/W gap until full roll. So require cross-version canary before wide rollout. 2) We can gate via feature-flag on route-level so Dedicated customers can opt in.

maria: Ops: what's the failure mode if new owner never sees settle_token because logs were truncated? We need stable-tail retention guarantees or a fallback.

alex: Two fallbacks: A) if logs truncated, owner A must attach a snapshot blob for the range up to settle_token during prepare; B) if snapshot transfer fails, abort handoff and keep old owner until human intervention. Both have cost tradeoffs. Suggest default to (A) limited to prefixes below some size threshold to avoid huge snapshots.

chen: Implementation complexity: we need to thread settle_token through sequencer, lease manager, and across RPCs. Also need to ensure prepare is idempotent in face of retries.

sam: Also think about eviction: demote and eviction interplay — if eviction is eager, we might choose to evict rather than transfer if settle_token indicates tiny tail. We should compare cost of transfer vs rehydrate later. Add heuristic: if size_of_pending <= threshold -> snapshot+transfer; else prefer eviction+rehydrate on demand.

ops-bot: deploy-bot: canary rollout scheduled: eng-runtime/canary-cluster @ 2024-04-22T14:00:00Z

maria: Sounds good. Last operational ask: add a canary dashboard that shows settle_token_gap and handoff success rate. We'll alert if read-after-write incidents > 0 for canary.

alex: I'll draft an RFC with handshake sketch, fallback policies, metrics, and test plan. Will include pseudocode and a compatibility matrix. tagging @chen @sam for review.

chen: Review early. Also add a short CLI debug endpoint to inspect settle_token for a prefix to help debugging in the field.

sam: +1. If we keep default conservative and add opt-in flags, we can ship safely. :thumbsup:
